title: Adaptive observability relay and namespace shielding for private deployments
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Problem: Private and Dedicated customers with co-located metric/log/trace agents report sporadic cross-namespace noise, opaque ingestion spikes, and unbounded memory growth in edge relays when tenants have bursty workloads. Existing collector isolation work focuses on sampling and quota enforcement but does not provide a lightweight, adaptive relay that can both shield namespaces and gracefully shed or reroute traffic without requiring full collector restarts.

Goal: Build an adaptive observability relay (lightweight sidecar/edge relay) for VPC/on-prem topologies that performs namespace-aware buffering, per-namespace backpressure, selective shedding, and safe replay markers. The relay should integrate with existing trusted identity headers and produce trace hooks compatible with our tracing pipeline so spans are anchored correctly across relays. Deliverables: design doc, reference implementation in Go, e2e test harness, dashboards for latency/error visibility, migration playbook for existing customers.
acceptance_criteria: Relay accepts telemetry with tenant namespace header and enforces a per-namespace memory cap without crashing
Burst protection: when a namespace exceeds configured token rate, relay applies probabilistic shedding and attaches a shed_reason attribute to events
Trace continuity: relay emits trace-hooks so parent/child relationships are preserved downstream even when events are shed and replayed
Replay-safe watermarking: relay marks persisted buffers with monotonic watermarks to avoid duplicate processing after failover
Dashboarding: new dashboards surface per-namespace ingest latency, shed-rate, and memory pressure with alert thresholds documented
No customer data leakage: namespaces are logically isolated; logs/traces from different namespaces do not mix in the relay buffer
design_decisions: Language: Go for minimal binary size and existing runtime libs for streaming
Buffering: use an append-only segmented buffer persisted to disk with size-limited segments to avoid OOM
Backpressure: implement token-bucket per-namespace with global fair-queueing to avoid starvation
Shedding policy: tiered approach — first apply sampling for low-priority events, then probabilistic full-event drops for sustained overload
Trace hooks: relay will propagate original trace ids and add a relay hop span with attribute relay.namespace and relay.shed_reason when applicable
Security: verify tenant identity via mTLS or signed identity header; reject mismatched identities
implementation_notes: Core relay lives as a single binary and can run as a daemonset in k8s or as a host agent for air-gapped installs
Configuration: central config via ConfigMap for k8s and a local yaml for on-prem; support dynamic config hot-reload
Metrics exported: expose prometheus metrics for namespace_queue_depth, namespace_shed_rate, relay_disk_usage, relay_uptime
Integration points: telemetry output to existing perimeter-forwarder and perimeter-telemetry-multiplexer via protobuf-over-TLS
Compatibility: must accept both OpenTelemetry and our legacy envelope format and normalize to a canonical internal wire format
rollout_plan: MVP alpha release to internal dogfood cluster (sprint+1)
Canary rollout to two low-risk Dedicated customers configured as non-blocking (observability-only) for 2 weeks
Collect metrics and iterate on shedding thresholds; follow-up patch to improve reproducibility of shed logs
Prepare migration playbook: how to swap existing collector with relay, rollback steps, expected downtime (none) and verification steps
Gradual enablement: enable for additional customers after 2 successful canaries and security review
test_plan: Unit tests for buffering and token-bucket enforcement
Load tests simulating bursty multi-namespace workloads with our perf harness
Chaos tests: simulate relay process OOM and disk full to verify replay and watermarking behavior
End-to-end tracing integration test verifying trace continuity through relay + downstream collector
Security tests for identity spoofing attempts and header/mTLS mismatches
